text:
The method about the method

Gradient descent proposes only what the local slope already recommends. It does not hold alternatives. It does not learn which alternatives were worth holding.

Change that. Let the model perturb itself. Not its weights. Its interventions: adapters, modules, routing tables, attention heads. Units that can be perturbed, scored and reverted as a block. Ten to the eleventh raw parameters is an appalling search space. A few thousand interventions is a tractable one.

The perturbations come from a distribution the model holds and revises. A frozen judge scores the results. Variation from inside, selection from outside.

No part of this is new. Evolution strategies perturb and select. CMA-ES learns its search distribution. Population Based Training perturbs configurations. The Darwin Gödel Machine keeps an archive and modifies its own modifier. What is new is the stack: model, proposal policy, policy update rule, judge. Every level can be made adaptive except the last one standing.

The interesting question is how the perturbation mechanism itself is set up and kept honest.

Initial optimization.

The first policy is designed, not learned. Someone chooses the action space. Someone chooses the initial distribution. Gradient disagreement is one natural prior: where local training signals conflict, give the proposal distribution more room; where they are stable, give it less. A prior, not a law of exploration, and available only while gradients are still being computed.

Someone chooses the judge. This choice sets the ceiling of everything above it. A test suite. A proof checker. A held-out task battery. A frozen model’s opinion, only if nothing better exists.

That is the bootstrap. The floor is built by hand.

Continuous optimization.

Two loops on two clocks.

The fast loop: perturb, judge, retain or revert. Keep an archive of everything tried, failures included. Ruin becomes a data point.

The slow loop: adjust the distribution the perturbations come from. Two objects carry it, center and spread. The center moves toward interventions that survived. The spread widens when the judge’s signal is flat and narrows when it is dense. Exploration is not a phase. It is a quantity, and it is tuned.

The slow loop has one more job: detect when the judge is saturated. Improvement against the judge stops predicting improvement on anything the judge did not see. From that moment, score improvement is indistinguishable from referee learning unless another judge confirms it.

Here is the trap. The moment the saturation test is used to change the policy, it joins the training signal. The held-out set is no longer held out. Goodhart moved up one floor. A genuinely external test must stay outside the loop or be continually renewed. Three roles, not two: selection signal, meta-selection signal, untouched audit. And when the audit feeds back, you need another one.

The regress.

The slow loop has parameters. Its update rule was written by someone. Evaluation recurses the same way: every judge that starts teaching stops being a judge. Every built system stops somewhere and freezes what remains: the judge, the meta-rule, the audit. That is the ceiling. Not a roof.

What changes is not that the regress ends. It is that each floor now costs an iteration instead of a substrate. The first floor is designed. The second is tuned. Above that, the method is whatever remains when the designer leaves the room.

The world’s first humanoid robot theater show just premiered in Shenzhen... even the host is a robot.

Fresh off street-dance gold at the second World Humanoid Robot Games, Lumos is taking its robots into a full stage production.

The 45-minute show features dance, sketch comedy, crosstalk, martial arts, DJ sets and magic. The NIX robots perform autonomously throughout, trading jokes with a child and helping a magician.

The hard part is keeping the robots and human cast in sync. Every entrance, line, gesture and transition has to happen on cue.

Shenzhen Culture and Tourism helped create the show and will run regular performances. This offers a working example for expanding the commercial use of humanoids in live entertainment.

text:
Pleased to join @SquawkCNBC to discuss the rise in bond yields and the Trump-Xi summit. Bond yields are reflecting the Fed pushing interest rates high due to its anti-growth models and the high demand for debt from AI and government spending. The Fed faces high oil prices spreading into core inflation and past years of plentiful/excess liquidity. The Fed is again losing hundreds of billions of dollar on its bond portfolio. Its demand-side models wrongly think the Fed can control inflation with high rates. On Squawk today, I argued that the U.S. is a supply-side economy, where prices are heavily influenced by production, innovation and the expected value of the dollar. To get yields down, it will be important to defend the dollar as China tries to gain market share for the yuan.
The U.S.-China meetings in Washington this week show that the U.S. is the stronger economy and the dollar the better currency, but that China has substantial leverage – through its strength in critical materials, fertilizer, food hoarding, chemicals, shipping lines, manufacturing, and flexible processing of fossil fuels. It has attached itself to Iran and the Global South through the BRICS, favorable treatment for Belt and Road debt, arms sales, sharing of satellite information, and strong influence in global institutions.
The U.S. needs to become less dependent on China for manufacturing, but that will take huge capital investments to reindustrialize, part of the upward pressure on bond yields. The Biden Administration left the government poorly positioned for this by shortening the US debt maturity, locking in high levels of federal spending, and ignoring the de-industrialization.
https://t.co/lqTXfYmoj9

text:
Intersect is at a turning point. This election will help decide whether it remains a status-quo organization that fades from relevance, or whether it finally forms a clear identity as a true member-based organization and builds toward lasting success, in the spirit of what the LFDT has achieved.

Intersect has delivered important work. Those results still do not, on their own, justify the current level of funding in the eyes of much of the community. Membership has fallen from 2–3k to just over 600. At $10 per membership, that decline is a clear signal: the organization has not yet earned durable member trust.

What Intersect needs now is operational expertise in running an MBO—not only community relations, and not only Cardano technical knowledge. It needs people who understand how to steward a nonprofit that delivers real member benefits, curates an ecosystem, and practices genuine open source.

To date, Intersect has only partly fulfilled those roles. Budget management and hard forks matter, but they are not the whole purpose of the organization, and they cannot be its only focus. The foundations still need to be planted.

I previously helped design and pilot the core functions Intersect needs in order to stabilize and grow. Much of that work has not been carried forward, and the ecosystem has felt the gap. If elected, I will put the connections, resources, and operating experience I have built over the past several years in service of the staff and the organization, so Intersect can deliver for members and set itself up to succeed. It is time to set the politics aside and see how bad the scarring on the hull really is…. 

Being on the outside I truly do see it and can guarantee I have more skin in this to see intersect succeed then most

text:
When people can enter the world and affect it, you need more than a good-looking scene. You need a story worth exploring, characters worth interacting with, and enough possibility to make people want to try something different just to see how the world responds.

With @PixVerse R2, the world keeps running while you’re inside it. You can move through the scene, steer the story, and change what happens with a prompt.

In one scene, I chose “Turn Back and Fight.” The monster fought back, and my character ended up getting kicked straight off a cliff.

That kind of cause and effect is what makes the experience feel different.

Until now, most AI video has still been built around finished outputs. You generate a clip, watch it, and if you want something different, you generate another one.

R2 turns that into something much closer to a live world.

And that changes what creators have to think about too.

Once the story can actually react to you, watching isn’t really passive anymore.

You start wondering less about what happens next, and more about what you could make happen next.

text:
The Full Story of $BUTT
Most memes are born, pump, die, and get forgotten in 48 hours.
$BUTT was supposed to be one of them.
It launched mid-September 2026 on Solana as a pure joke: Bittensor = decentralized intelligence. Buttensor = decentralized stupidity. Two cheeks. “No thoughts. Just $BUTT.” Paired against TAO with a 3% tax that buys and distributes real $TAO straight to holders.
It pumped hard. Then it got completely destroyed.
The original dev either vanished or refused to hand over the X account when the community tried to take control. At that point $BUTT should have been dead. Almost every token in that situation is.
But a few people refused to let it die.
One of the loudest early holders stepped up and volunteered his personal account because the original one was locked. He’s said it publicly many times: “I’m not the dev. There is no current dev. I’m just a holder who’s biased as hell because I believe in this thing.”
The community took full ownership of $BUTT. No team. No roadmap. No CEO of Ass. Just people who decided the joke was still worth keeping alive.
And the mechanism never stopped working.
Every buy, sell, and transfer of $BUTT still takes a 3% tax. That tax still buys real $TAO. That $TAO still gets sent to $BUTT holders.
Since launch they have already distributed nearly $1 million worth of $TAO this way.
They call it Proof of Cheeks.
What started as the dumbest possible meme slowly turned into something stranger: a Trojan horse. People show up for the ass. They stay because $TAO starts appearing in their wallet. Some of them eventually ask the dangerous question: “Wait… what the fuck is TAO actually?”
And just like that, a Solana trench animal falls into the Bittensor rabbit hole — all because they held $BUTT.
They even built a whole philosophy around it called BUTT/ACC (Butt Accelerationism):
Bittensor decentralizes intelligence. $BUTT decentralizes stupidity. Culture is the last unofficial subnet. A meme should outlive its creator.
The people still holding $BUTT aren’t waiting for a new main character. They’re just holding the ass, collecting TAO, and slowly turning a dead joke into a living onboarding machine for decentralized AI.
No one owns it. No one is in charge. $BUTT belongs to whoever is still here.
That’s the entire story.
No thoughts. Just $BUTT.
